title: GHEC Discovery Collector Common Execution Profile
description: Normative baseline execution profile and shared requirements for all GHEC discovery collectors.

outputEnvelope.description: Common envelope format for normalized evidence records produced by discovery collectors.

id.description: Immutable, opaque namespaced identifier for the evidence record.

scopeRef.description: Hierarchical resource anchor linking the record to its enclosing scope.

id.description: Unique identifier of the parent scope resource.

collectorExecutionId.description: Identifier of the specific collector execution that observed this record.

operation.description: Reviewed collector or operation ID (e.g. rest.orgs.get).

privacy.description: Normative privacy boundaries, prohibited data categories, and redaction rules.

pseudonymization.keyRetention: discard key upon bundle publication; do not persist identity mapping

invariants: No collector may execute an endpoint whose response schema contains prohibited data unless a documented metadata-only parameter exists.
Filtering out prohibited fields in-memory after receiving them from GitHub is strictly forbidden.
The minimal redaction profile does not bypass prohibited categories.
Sensitive opt-in metadata flags never permit secret or credential retrieval.

outcomes.description: Standardized terminal outcome taxonomy for collector executions.

states.complete: All target resources in the scoped denominator were successfully enumerated with full coverage and zero errors.
states.partial: Some target resources were enumerated, but coverage was bounded by pagination limits, partial visibility, or non-fatal errors.
states.failed: The collector encountered a fatal error (e.g. 401 authentication failure, network disconnect) and produced no usable evidence.
states.skipped: The collector was not executed because required parent resource anchors (e.g. repository list) were missing or skipped.
states.unavailable: The target capability is disabled by policy, unsupported on the plan, or inaccessible due to verified permission boundaries.

http.description: HTTP transport, error handling, rate limiting, and retry policies.

rateLimiting.primary: Honor Retry-After and x-ratelimit-reset headers; apply exponential backoff with full jitter.
rateLimiting.secondary: Detect secondary throttling (403/429 with throttling message); back off immediately with minimum 60-second delay.
rateLimiting.budget: Halt further requests and finalize collector as partial if operator request budget is exceeded.

errorHandling.200: Success; parse JSON response according to allowlisted output fields.
errorHandling.204: Success with empty body; record presence/absence indicator.
errorHandling.301: Follow redirect only within api.github.com domain; never follow redirects to external download URLs.
errorHandling.302: Redirect; block if pointing to an archive, binary download, or report generation URL.
errorHandling.304: Not modified; valid for conditional/cached requests.
errorHandling.401: Unauthorized / Bad credentials; fail scan immediately with sanitized error; do not retry.
errorHandling.403: Forbidden; inspect reason (permission denial vs secondary throttle). Never retry permission denials; mark capability unavailable or partial.
errorHandling.404: Not found or inaccessible; record as missing/inaccessible resource; do not retry. In enterprise scope, 404 does not prove absence.
errorHandling.422: Unprocessable entity; indicates invalid query parameters or unsupported resource state; record sanitized error.
errorHandling.429: Too many requests; back off per rate limit policy.
errorHandling.5xx: Server error; retry transient failures with exponential backoff up to maxAttempts.
